The fourth industrial revolution has accelerated advances in technology and widened the digital landscape. Consequently,
cybercrime remains a growing threat for financial fraud and unauthorised access to customer information. While there are
numerous threats aimed at bank systems and their customers, one of the biggest threats, and, often one of the hardest to
detect, is that originated by, or done in collaboration with, malicious and compromised staff.
Impact: Cybersecurity has become a paramount concern for the banking sector, leading to increased investments in counter
measures including technology and processes on how banks operate.
Response: Continuous heavy investments in cybersecurity infrastructure, people skills and training to identify and neutralise
threats, prevent data breaches and other forms of cyber-attacks. The Bank carries out enhanced penetration tests on its systems
using in-house ethical hackers and externally sourced skilled experts.
